# Eretz Yisrael lesson 7 in 3D - "The Great Sea that guards the coast": brief for the builders

Source: lesson 7 of the Toldot Eretz Yisrael series (source text C:/projects/toldot-eretz-yisrael/v2/content/lesson07.json, section b). The 2D version was delivered on 19/10/2026; Yosef asked for a LONGER and richer 3D version, in the style of lesson 6 3D (productions/toldot06) and the new pipeline (skill video-production).
Audience: Haredi boys, about 6th grade (12 years old). Shown in class on a projector with music and NO narration: the captions are the explanation. Men and boys only, modest clothes, no crosses/churches/mosques.
Engine, API, gestures, worker rules: references/builder_kit.md of the skill (read it first). Page head: copy productions/azamra342/_head_example.html. Characters: BOY and RAV look constants are written ONCE in productions/toldot07/shared.js by the first builder and imported by everyone (BOY = student, scale .72, kippa; RAV = teacher with beard and glasses).
Output: productions/toldot07/film_b.html (parts: _part_film_b_N.html, each part <= 60 s).

## Series: BANNED line (grows after each first render)
- No flat blue board for the sea: the sea is always a rolling 3D surface (pure function of t) with foam and a light glint.
- No still hold longer than 1 s: the camera moves, never the caption.
- No character floating or sinking; feet on sand/deck/floor.
- No Math.random/Date: use rng(seed). No hat except kippa/none.

## Look constants (numbers, not adjectives)
Palette: sea shallow #52c0e0, sea deep #1f78b4, foam #ffffff, sand #f0d9a8, sky top #7fcdf3, sky bottom #fff1cf, hero red (bottle) #e5473c, gold #f2c14e, ink outline #1c2b3a, outline width 0.03 m. Light: warm sun from the west, 25-35 degrees above the horizon, colour #ffe2a6, soft shadows. Ease: arrive=out, camera=io, exit=in; exits 40-50 % shorter than entrances; a new element starts when the previous one is 30-50 % done.
Central visual metaphor of the series: THE SEA IS A GUARDED BORDER - the wave RUNS but the water STAYS. Film b hero object: THE BOTTLE - a big translucent red glass bottle with a gold cap (about 0.35 m long) that rides every wave and never travels sideways. A thin gold dashed vertical line through the bottle shows "it did not move sideways".
Shared sea: productions/toldot07/sea.js (built ONCE by the first builder, imported by all): sea(Wd, {amp: t=>m, wavelength, speed, dir, shallow, deep, size}) returns {heightAt(x,z,t)}, a rolling toon surface with foam crests; objects that float (bottle, boat, buoy) take their y from heightAt and keep x,z (bottle orbit radius <= 0.08 m). Also beach(Wd, {slope}) = a sloping sand strip with a wet line; wave-on-slope helper that curls, breaks to foam and runs up the sand, then soaks away.

## Accuracy notes (supervisor checked against the source text)
- Wave heights: summer about 0.5 m, sometimes 1 m (from memory in the source, rounded); ordinary winter storm 3-4 m; more than 6 m = "significant wave height" in the strongest storms measured by buoys off Ashdod and Haifa. The 6 m is shown AT SEA, never on the beach (fidelity review fix).
- Verses on screen: Tehillim 107:25, Tehillim 93:4 (the single phrase), Yirmeyahu 5:22. Gemara: Yevamot 121a, Bava Batra 73a. Rashi (Yirmeyahu 5:22, on "haotti lo tira'u"): paraphrase with "<LBL_TXT_01>" and NO quotation marks.
- The weather/storm date is as in the source: Tevet 5771 (December 2010), the protective wall at Caesarea beach was damaged.
- No crane, rope-wave or hand-shaking-a-rope image (source note: a rope wave needs a hand). No exact tide figures.
